chosen.title: The Binary Threshold
chosen.idea: A high-precision split layout dividing the canvas into two discrete technical zones along an exact vertical seam: Left pane displays 'HEALTHY [HF > 1.100]' with stable collateral ratios and nominal debt telemetry; Right pane displays 'LIQUIDATION CANDIDATE [HF <= 1.100]' showing an immediate air-gapped containment barrier with four sequential validation gates (Oracle, Config, Funding, Execution) locked in place to isolate contagion before bad debt touches the system.
chosen.why: This is the recommended concept because it cleanly dramatizes the mathematical binary at the heart of the mechanism: solvency is not a gradient on Vanna, but an enforced structural boundary separating active positions from isolated liquidation candidates.

all.title: The 1.100 Datum Line
all.idea: A stark, architectural layout dominated by the oversized metric '1.100 HF' rendered in monolithic tabular numerals. A razor-sharp technical datum line cuts horizontally through the canvas directly beneath the number, with precise micro-annotations indicating the exact inflection point where debt exposure ceases to be considered healthy and enters immediate protocol-enforced containment.
all.why: Distills the protocol's risk philosophy into a single unyielding number that institutional risk desks can instantly parse and remember as the hard floor against undercollateralization.

all.title: The Reality of Borrowing
all.idea: An austere editorial layout leading with the hook in heavy, uncompromising sans-serif: 'Leverage is easy. Not getting liquidated is the hard part.' Directly below the statement, an austere monospace technical panel outlines Vanna's structural answer: a hard floor at strictly > 1.10 HF with automated candidate isolation.
all.why: Cuts through standard crypto hype by acknowledging the trader's actual operational anxiety, positioning Vanna's automated containment as the institutional antidote to unexpected liquidations.
